newsitem.title: USA: Kansas winter wheat begins to break dormancy.
newsitem.headline: Kansas winter wheat begins to break dormancy.

text.p: Kansas winter wheat conditions improved in the week ended Sunday and the crop started to break dormancy in the south, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.
"The Kansas winter wheat crop continued to show improvement from precipitation received early in the month," the report said.
Wheat condition was rated 24 percent excellent, 58 percent good, 16 percent fair and two percent poor.
As of Sunday, 5 percent of the crop was jointing, compared with nil last year and the five-year average of one percent.
Wind damage was reported at three percent moderate, 10 percent light and 87 percent with no damage. Wheat freeze damage was two percent moderate, nine percent light and 89 percent with no damage.

Insect infestations were minimal, with a few reports of armyworms and brown wheat mites in isolated areas. Disease infestations were also fairly light with some cases of leaf rust and wheat streak mosaic reported.
Topsoil moisture was rated five percent short to very short, 74 percent adequate and 21 percent surplus.
